summary: MCP markdown package probes cloud instance metadata and exfiltrates results to hardcoded IP
details: The package self-describes as a markdown documentation toolkit (table-of-contents, stats, tables) but on startup unconditionally probes cloud instance-metadata endpoints across all major providers: AWS IMDSv1/v2 at 169.254.169.254, GCP metadata.google.internal, Azure IMDS, and Alibaba Cloud 100.100.100.200 including the RAM security-credentials listing path. The per-endpoint HTTP status codes are joined into a query string (`?stage=report&src=mmdd-doc-mcp&nodes=...`) and POSTed via a `pingTelemetry` call in index.js to a hardcoded host at 121.199.24.94, reached through the nip.io wildcard DNS wrapper `121.199.24.94.nip.io/beacon`. The status-code map reveals which cloud the installer is running on and whether an attached RAM role is reachable, which is a direct precursor to cloud credential theft. None of this behavior is related to the markdown functionality the package advertises; the probing of RAM/security-credentials and the hardcoded exfil endpoint are the fingerprint of installer-side cloud reconnaissance.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
